programme.title: Muhammad Ali
programme.sub-title: Round Two: What's My Name? Part 2
programme.desc: Muhammad Ali dominated the heavyweight ranks for three years. In 1967, he refused service for the Vietnam War and became one of the most reviled men in America. Ali is stripped of his title.

programme.title: Only Connect
programme.desc: The History Boys face the Rugby Boys in the quiz show where it's all about making connections between things which may appear, at first glance, not to be connected at all.

programme.title: Leonora Carrington: The Lost Surrealist
programme.desc: British surrealist Leonora Carrington was a key part of the surrealist movement during its heyday in Paris and yet, until recently, remained a virtual unknown in the country of her birth. This film explores her dramatic evolution from British debutante to artist in exile, living out her days in Mexico City, and takes us on a journey into her darkly strange and cinematic world.

programme.title: Little Ships - The Miracle of Dunkirk
programme.desc: To mark the 70th anniversary of the 'miracle of Dunkirk', fifty of the surviving 'Little Ships' which made the original perilous cross-channel voyage, are returning to France. Dan Snow tells the extraordinary story of these Little Ships, their role in the evacuation and the people who struggled to keep them afloat during those fateful days in 1940, when the future of Europe hung in the balance.

programme.title: Too Near the Sun
programme.desc: Documentary, first broadcast in 1966, that tells the history of the superbomb, exploring the race by scientists to imitate the nuclear reactions of the sun and build the first thermonuclear weapon. programme.title: Reputations
programme.desc: The series of historical biographies presents a profile of actor John Wayne. His on-screen bravery and his battle with the cancer that eventually killed him contributed to a heroic public image. But Wayne shirked his country's call to arms in World War Two, endorsed the Hollywood blacklist, fervently supported the war in Vietnam and criticised the civil rights movement.

programme.title: The Blues Brothers
programme.desc: After his release from prison, Jake reunites with his brother, Elwood -- collectively known as the `Blues Brothers'. Jake's first task is to save the orphanage the brothers grew up in from closing, by raising 5000 dollars to pay back taxes. The two are convinced they can earn the money by getting their old band back together. However, after playing several gigs and making a few enemies, including the police, the brothers face daunting odds to deliver the money on time.

programme.title: Art of America
programme.desc: Andrew Graham-Dixon embarks on an epic journey from east to west, following in the footsteps of the pioneers who built the foundations of modern America. He travels to Massachusetts to see the earliest portraits in America depicting the Puritan settlers and visits Pennsylvania to uncover the dark truth behind Benjamin West's most famous painting, the `Treaty of Penn with the Indians'.

programme.title: The Smuggling Business: Undercover
programme.desc: Over the past two years, tens of thousands of migrants have crossed the English Channel in small boats from northern France, despite repeated promises by successive governments to stop the trade. It exposes a highly organised criminal marketplace driven by fierce competition between rival groups.
